turns.question: For returns dated 1 or 2 October 2026, what was the median number of days between the original order date and the return date?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no such metric for the median days between order date and return date; the closest metrics are returns_count (Returns) and returns_eur (Returns (EUR)).

turns.question: On 1 and 2 October 2026, how much larger in EUR was the average amount of returns with reason damaged than of returns with reason wrong size?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no such metric for the average amount of a return; the closest metrics are returns_eur (Returns (EUR)) and returns_count (Returns), which can be filtered by return reason.

turns.question: For leads that turned into a booking in September 2026, what was the median number of days from lead creation to booking?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no such metric for the median days from lead creation to booking; the closest metrics are lead_to_booking_rate (Lead-to-booking rate), leads and bookings.

turns.question: Which day of the week had the highest average daily ad spend across all campaigns in September 2026, and what was that average in EUR?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no such metric for ad spend by day of the week (only day, week, month and year grains exist); the closest metric is ad_spend_eur (Ad spend (EUR)), which can be grouped by day.

turns.question: In sessions between 20 September and 3 October 2026 that had both an add-to-cart and a checkout, what was the median number of minutes from the first add-to-cart to the checkout?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no such metric for the median minutes from add-to-cart to checkout; the closest metrics are cart_to_checkout_rate (Cart-to-checkout rate), cart_sessions and checkout_sessions.

turns.question: Which customer opened the most CRM emails between 20 September and 3 October 2026, and how many did they open?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no such metric for email opens per customer; the closest metric is customer_actions (Customer actions), which can be split by action type (email_open) but not ranked by individual customer.

turns.question: At which hour of the day did the most checkout events happen between 20 September and 3 October 2026, and how many were there in that hour?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no such metric for checkouts by hour of the day (the finest grain is the day); the closest metrics are checkout_sessions (Checkout sessions) and customer_actions filtered to the checkout action type.

turns.question: For outreach messages sent between 20 September and 3 October 2026 that got a reply, what was the 75th percentile of hours between the message and the reply?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no such metric for the 75th percentile of hours between a message and its reply; the closest metrics are messages_sent, messages_replied, replies and reply_rate.

turns.question: For candidates who reached the interview stage between 30 September and 4 October 2026, what was the median number of days from their application to the interview stage?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no such metric for the median days from application to interview stage; the closest metrics are applications, candidates_in_stage (Candidates in stage) and time_to_hire_days (Time to hire (days)).

turns.question: What was the ratio of non-cancelled order revenue to total ad spend in September 2026?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no such metric for a ratio of revenue to ad spend; the closest metrics are revenue_eur (Revenue (EUR)) and ad_spend_eur (Ad spend (EUR)), which can each be asked for September 2026 separately.

turns.question: How many site sessions were there per order placed between 20 September and 2 October 2026?
turns.answer: The semantic layer has no such metric for sessions per order; the closest metrics are site_sessions (Site sessions) and orders_total (Orders), which can each be asked for the period separately.
